rows: Envy
Hate
Vipers; poppies with heads nipped off (Ovid). Starlings kept as a house behaviour
a house that is always looking next door, all windows angled outward, every room a copy of somewhere grander.
a pinacotheca of empty painted-panel recesses, each with a small bronze titulus naming a picture that hangs in someone else's house.

(C) Every doorway frames the next room, which is always a little brighter and warmer than yours. • (C) A second footfall follows yours, half a beat late, as if someone next door is trying your steps on.

(C) Bronze-ringed peepholes at eye height in walls, doors and cupboard backs, each looking into a lit room you cannot reach; more appear as Envy grows. • (C) Mirrors that improve what they reflect: the rug thicker, the fire taller, your cloak hanging in better folds. • (U: first time the player covets something a guest or rival owns) The house copies it overnight; a guest's walking staff reappears in the tall amphora by the door, polished higher. One copy per such act.

(C, pervasive) Across the wing, rooms resize so wherever you stand is the smaller room; ceilings sit a hand lower than the next, corridors stretch toward whoever just left. • (U: crossing into Deep) Glossy starlings arrive all at once and roost along the cornices, mimicking guests' voices a room away. • (U: stages, one per rival surpassed or lost to) Raised relief creeps over the plaster: the floor plan of a grander house, one wing traced per stage, never finished.
the peepholes stay, each stopped with wax, and one bronze mirror has a patch rubbed dull.
Mirrors improve the room, not you
Good will
Love
Halcyon; elm wound with vine
a house built to receive, with a seat for whoever arrives and a lamp left burning.
a wax-tablet diptych on a stand by the door, always open to a freshly smoothed leaf, a stylus beside it.
(C) Chairs stand slightly pulled out from tables, as if someone just rose to make room. • (U: any approach to the house) An oil lamp is lit in the nearest window.

(C) Wooden pegs by the door multiply to match the guests, each with a small bronze tag bearing a Greek numeral. • (C) Doors open a moment before a hand reaches them, then rest ajar. • (U: first time the player shelters a stranger) A sleek, unhurried house cat arrives and settles beside whoever sits alone longest.

(C, pervasive) A current of warm, bread-scented air drifts toward wherever people gather; corridors between occupied rooms shorten until every route ends at the long kitchen table. • (U: one per bond formed) A place card appears on that table bearing that person's name in a round hand, laid before they next arrive. • (C) An open-hand motif recurs: on lintels, pressed into bread with a bread stamp, cast in the bronze of the gate.
a hollow worn into the doorstep, and one chair left pulled out that nobody sits in.
Owns the house cat (Malleability, Shamelessness and Injustice gave theirs up).
Greed
Hope
Thin wolf; knotted purse; toad under the hearthstone (Ripa)
a treasure house still being filled, every shelf stocked and every room planned for more.
an unfinished extension, scaffolding inside the house, with rooms framed but empty and a notice painted on the plaster: "next year".
(C) A soft chink of coin behind the walls, as if something is being counted. • (C) Padlocks on things that need none: a bread crock, a sewing basket, a window seat.

(U: crossing into Marked) A fat toad settles under the hearthstone and slowly grows fatter; it never finishes its food, leaving a small heap of earth beside it in case the earth runs out. • (U: one per acquisition) A tally mark is scored into the nearest door frame. • (C) Every empty niche holds a sherd scratched "to be filled".

(C, pervasive) Each vivid, Loose memory's lamp is locked in its own bronze-bound strongbox, or a wall niche behind a bronze grille, where it sits in whichever emotion's wing; bronze hinges, hasps and corner plates appear on these only. Air drifts towards the nearest one, doors swing shut behind you on its side, and loose things creep a little closer to it each visit; floors creak a running tally of what you hold. • (U: each time a large treasure is won) A new door appears overnight onto a narrow closet, already shelved and awaiting stock.
felt-lined niches still holding the pressed shape of what was taken, and a ring of bronze keys that open nothing.

Toad from Ripa's Avarice. The hoard is vivid, Loose memories, locked where they sit (memories stay in their emotion's wing). Locks possessions (Obduracy locks doors). Guests' things belong to Envy, not Greed.
Generosity
Joy
Overflowing cornucopia
a house that keeps spilling out of itself, gifts on every sill and nothing kept behind glass.
a doorstep shelf of small cloth bundles tied with cord, each with a friend's name scratched on a sherd tied to the knot, waiting to go out (Inspect: "Wrapped. Not yet given."); some hold small lamps.
(C) Crumbs on the outer sills, and sparrows that come for them. • (C) A spare cloak and a broad straw sun hat always hang by the door.

(U: first gift given freely) A lemon-scented herb takes root from a dropped cutting; after that it spreads continuously, pots on every sill labelled "take one". • (C) Windows stand open, small birds passing through freely. • (C) There is always one spare cup on the hook and one spare chair at the table, ready for a guest.

(C, pervasive) A gentle outward breeze runs through the house toward the front door, carrying petals, seeds and loose ribbon; rooms by the door are full, inner rooms pleasantly bare. • (U: stages, one per great sacrifice) A non-load-bearing partition (one that adds no capacity and holds no memories or beliefs) comes down and is carried outside as a trestle table; rooms widen and open up, but never merge. • (U: crossing into Deep) Every guest leaves with something in their pocket: a warm bun, a smooth pebble, a folded note.
string loops still hanging from the beams where gifts were tied, and a lined basket by the door, waiting.
Keeps the sparrows (Humility's sparrow needs a replacement). Only cosmetic partitions come down. Eagle dropped as an emblem.
Cruelty
Hate
Tiger
a house that tests whoever walks it, every surface honed and every threshold a small trial.
a single exquisite bronze-legged chair in the hall, its fine wool cushion with a bronze needle standing upright in it.
(C) Every rose in every vase carries one perfect, prominent thorn. • (C) Floor tiles stay silent except when you are trying to be quiet.

(C) A carved stone balustrade of thorned bramble scroll climbs the stairs, then real briars, trained and immaculate, along the garden walls. • (U: first time the player wounds the defenceless) A shrike nests on the gate; each later such act adds a trinket impaled on the bronze finials, arranged with care. • (C) Chairs tilt forward, pressing the sitter to sit straight. • (C) A tiger-skin rug lies before the main hearth, head still on, its glass eyes catching the firelight.

(C, pervasive) Hoar frost spreads in fine crystalline needles, cold and dazzling, silencing the wing and biting any hand laid flat. • (U: crossing into Deep) The house herds visitors: doors close firmly behind them and corridors realign to lead guests, politely, to a blank wall. • (U: one per humiliation inflicted) A bronze lamp-wheel strung with shards of broken glass vessels is hung in a hall; all of them ring thinly whenever someone stumbles.
tiny holes in every cushion where the needles stood, and finials filed blunt, a burr still on them.
Owns thorns (Defiance keeps only thistles). Diamond heart dropped as an emblem.
Mercifulness
Grief
Olive
a house that softens every fall, low and quiet, with somewhere to sit down wherever you need to.
a broken vase set back together with soft cloth binding, kept on a cushion in a lit niche.
(C) A soft blanket appears over whatever you have just left behind. • (C) Anything that falls falls slowly, landing without a sound.

(C) Sharp edges are found wrapped in soft cloth bindings, corner by corner. • (C) Doors close softly on their own, never latching hard. • (U: first time the player spares a beaten foe) Benches begin to appear along any corridor where someone tires. • (C) An olive tree grows in the Grief courtyard.

(C, pervasive) Springy moss creeps over stone, flags and stairs throughout the wing, cushioning steps and drinking echoes. • (U: crossing into Deep) A Quiet Room opens off the cellar landing, curtains drawn; anyone hurt who enters the house is led there. • (U: one per wrong forgiven) Stairs ease into ramps, one flight per act, starting with the cellar stair. • (C) A fine, cool mist hangs at head height, softening glare and blurring hard outlines.
smooth patches of stone where the moss was lifted, and cloth bindings still tied around things long since mended.
Owns moss (Humility to drop its moss). Moths given up for cloth bindings. Pelican and thunderbolt dropped as emblems.
Falseness
Fear
Mask (as traces only: painted fronts, not literal masks)
a theatre-set house of beautiful surfaces, false doors and painted depths, where nothing is quite where it seems.
a window with a painted view so perfect that it is the most beautiful window in the house, and it does not open.
a water clock that drips steadily while its float never rises (C); a fine vase that rings hollow when brushed, a painted shell (U: first lie told to an ally).

occasionally, while you are out of view, a corridor gains a painted false door, never a real one, so the layout stays true; an inner voice notices it as you pass ("You counted six doors on the way in. There are seven."), a little more often with depth (C). Painted oil lamps on painted brackets glow on the plaster and give light but cast no shadows (Inspect: "The flame is painted. The light is not."); one is added for every successful deception (U: per deed). Echoes come back half a beat late, not quite in the player's voice (C).

the house rehearses. Leave a room and return, and it has been reset like a stage between acts; just out of sight, furniture scrapes and stagehand footsteps hurry off (C, pervasive across the Fear wing, creeping into corridors everywhere). Mirrors lag a breath behind their subject (U: crossing into Deep). The Façade Wing, a flawless set of rooms that unfolds only for guests while the real rooms close behind painted flats (U: first time the player hides something from a visiting guest). Moths patterned exactly like the painted plaster's sheen lift off the walls when looked at (C).

flats stacked against bare plaster, slack ropes in the rafters, a false door with its painting half scraped away; the water clock's float now rises, but the hour line it should reach is still painted on.
Keeps the camouflage moths (Cowardice and Shame moths still to resolve). Masks swapped for painted sconces; cuttlefish dropped.
Fidelity
Love
Dog
a house that keeps its word: every door leads where it promises, every material is what it looks like, and things stay where they were left.
a pair of keys hung together on one hook, both polished from use, neither ever missing.
a bronze bell by the door that rings the same note every time (C); a bronze water heater always warm at the edge of the brazier (U: first promise kept at a cost).

a path wears glossy into the stone and mosaic along the routes the player always walks, deepening with every return (C). A pair of swallows nests in the eaves, there on every visit (U: crossing into Marked). A lamp burns in one window for a named companion; one more lamp per sworn bond (U: per bond sworn). An old dog waits by the door, awake, and is always there when the player returns (C).

the house waits. Every room ever visited keeps a lamp lit and a chair turned toward the door, and doors open at the player's step in the same order every time (C, pervasive through the whole house). Ivy follows a single faithful route along the walls, rooted into the mortar, holding the stones together (C). The Keeping Room, where each oath fulfilled hangs as a carved Herakles knot (U: room opens on crossing into Deep; knots added per fulfilled oath). Returning guests find their cup exactly where they left it, still warm (C).
one key alone on the double hook; the glossy path still leads to a door that now stays shut; an empty swallows' nest.

Keeps one named window lamp per bond (check Nobility's lamp). The old dog is awake and waiting, unlike the sleeping hounds of Despondency and Baseness. Ring dropped; the lovers' knots carry it. The polished track needs a record of where you walk.
Pride
Joy
Peacock; mirrors
a gleaming hall built to be seen, high and bright, every surface showing off its owner's triumphs.
a scroll on a stand, lit from above, unrolled to the best column of the owner's deeds.
footsteps echo back slightly louder, like a ripple of applause (C); a laurel wreath worked into the handle of one door (U: first public triumph).

a bronze plaque engraved with each great deed appears in a room (U: per deed). Doors open on a resonant chime, swelling with depth (C). A bronze automaton peacock fans its tail when the player enters (U: crossing into Marked). Mirrors show the player a little larger, standing among their achievements (C).

the house turns toward the player. Statues' heads follow them and ceilings lift as they cross a threshold (C, pervasive through the Joy wing and every grand space). Trophy halls multiply, each case larger than the last (C). The Hall of Audience, with a raised gallery where guests are seated to watch the player (U: first time a guest praises the player aloud).
empty plinths with only the statues' feet left; scaffolding under a cracked dome; plaques with names chiselled out, the outlines still catching the light; the peacock jammed half-fanned.

Mirrors show you larger, among your achievements. Hall of Audience is a gallery of admiration, not command. Pride is deeds, Vanity is looks: the following spotlight and the portrait galleries belong to Vanity, Pride has trophies. Keeps the peacock (Vanity's tail bird to become the jackdaw).
Humility
Calm
Mirror with a hairline crack
a low, quiet house of plain good things, sized to the body, nothing asking to be looked at.
a single, slightly lopsided handmade bowl in the place of honour, used daily.
thresholds worn into a gentle dip (C); a spider's web left untouched in a kitchen corner, the house sharing itself with small things (U: first credit given away to another).

doorways lower, so everyone bows a little to pass (C). Brooms and aprons hang by the doors; a new tool appears each time the player does menial service unasked (U: per deed). Other people's voices carry a touch clearer than the player's own (C). Mirrors show the player exactly as they are, each with a hairline crack (C).

the house makes room. Stools and benches appear as guests arrive, and the player's own image is nowhere: mirrors are taken down one by one, leaving pale rectangles on the limewash (on an outer wall, a small window onto the kitchen garden may take their place), and portraits show other people (C, pervasive across the house). Herb pots gather on sills and steps (C). A settled hush like steady breathing fills the centre, and corridors shorten to bring the player where needed (U: crossing into Deep). The Common Table, a long plain board with a bowl for everyone ever helped (U: opens the first time the player accepts help).
a single high-backed chair where the stool stood, a little too large for the room; wooden bowls stacked and unused; dry, empty herb pots on one step.

Mirrors show you as you are, with a hairline crack; at Deep they come down. Moss belongs to Mercifulness. Common Table opens on accepting help (no longer shares the declined-reward trigger). Lamb dropped.
Defiance
Courage
Claw marks
a fortress-house braced against the weather, thick walls, sharp angles and doors that face the storm.
a battered shield fixed above the hearth, every dent kept, none hammered out.
a weathervane that always points into the wind (C); a draught under every door that never stops (U: first refusal of a powerful figure).
shutters bang and the walls shudder under the wind outside, harder with depth (C). Doors push back against the hand, then give all at once with a bang (U: crossing into Marked).

a standing storm wraps the house; rain lashes the outer walls and they never give (C, pervasive over the exterior; the storm never comes inside). Every wound survived adds a kept scar to a wall (U: per defeat survived without yielding). The house answers how it is met: run, and corridors lengthen; stand your ground, and they shorten (U: crossing into Deep). Ravens on the parapet face the gale, and thistles break from the cracks (C). Guests find the gate shut until they knock three times (C).
the storm blows out and leaves a silent rampart; the shield's dents hammered flat, badly; the weathervane seized, pointing at a wind that no longer comes.
Storm stays outside (Audacity owns indoor storms). Keeps only thistles (Cruelty owns thorns). Bear dropped.
Despondency
Despair
Leafless tree; lodestone that will not settle (Pliny)
a sunken, hushed house of soft collapse, where everything has quietly settled downward into stillness.
a window seat piled with cushions, looking out on endless gentle rain.
a seeping amphora that drips very slowly, slower with depth (C); cushions still holding the shape of someone who has just stood up (U: first quest abandoned).

a soft indoor drizzle falls in one room, spreading to more rooms with depth (C). Dropped things roll gently downhill toward the cellar (C). Water clocks run dry, one for each goal given up (U: per abandoned goal), and shallow puddles that never dry lie as still mirrors on the floor (C). A sliver of lodestone floats on water in a bronze bowl, turning and never coming to rest (C).

the house sinks. Still water rises in the cellars and the lowest rooms become calm pools mirroring their ceilings; stairs up lengthen and stairs down shorten (C, pervasive through the lower house). A vast sleeping hound lies across one threshold, never waking, and must be stepped over (U: crossing into Deep). Snails leave silvery trails on the walls, and guests' voices sink to a murmur as they enter (C). A leafless tree stands in the Despair courtyard (C).
a tide line on the walls marking where the water stood; warped floorboards; a hound-shaped hollow pressed into a rug.
Owns the sleeping hound (Baseness has the pig instead). Water clocks run dry one per goal given up, distinct from Inflexibility's fixed sundials. Soft drizzle stays; Audacity owns indoor storms.
Imperiousness
Love
The throne
a court built to be adored, where every axis runs to one raised seat and the house expects you to approach.
a bronze gong on a stand beside the throne, whose single struck note every door in the house answers.

(C) In the Love wing's main room, one chair stands a little taller than the rest. • (C) A rope of heavy braided cord across one Love-wing doorway; it unhooks only for the owner. • (C) In neighbouring rooms, one chair has quietly turned toward the tall chair.

(C) The tall chair rises onto a dais. • (U: first time crossing into Marked) A herald's echo: entering a room, the player hears their own name announced a beat ahead of their footsteps. • (C) The owner's seal ring is pressed into wax on every door and chest, until the whole house reads as sealed. • (U: each time the player makes a companion wait or defer) An antechamber appears before an important room, with a waiting bench and a door that opens after a pause.

(U: crossing into Deep) The dais gets a room of its own and the chair becomes a true throne. • (C, pervasive) The corridors of the whole house bend toward the dais. Any route, taken long enough, ends at the throne. • (U: in stages, one per companion who submits or swears loyalty) A court of faceless, softly robed attendants lines the walls, bowing as you pass. • (C) Light gathers brightest at the throne, leaving guests a half step in shadow.
the throne turned to face a blank wall; the wax seals crumbled from every door; gongs and bells hanging silent, their clappers gone.

Owns the throne, staged: taller chair (Early), dais (Growing), own room and true throne (Deep); corridors bend to it. Light gathers at the throne, not on the player (Vanity owns the following spotlight). Crown and yoke dropped.
Meekness
Grief
Bowed reed
a low, yielding cottage where every room makes way and the best chair is always kept for someone else.
a plumped guest armchair by the hearth that nobody sits in, beside a worn stool that is clearly the owner's.
(C) Doors swing gently away from you before you touch them, as if stepping aside. • (C) Felt pads under every leg; nothing in the house ever scrapes.

(U: the first time the player yields a reward or a choice to another) A small wren arrives and nests in low corners, hopping out of your path rather than flying. • (C) Furniture edges back toward the walls whenever anyone enters. • (C) Vases of reeds whose heads are always bowed.

(C, pervasive) Hard corners, newels and sills are rubbed smooth and round by years of people brushing past as they step aside, spreading out from the Grief wing until the house cannot bruise. • (U: triggered per guest visit) Ceilings ease lower and the owner's rooms shrink so the guest rooms grow.
pale rubbed tracks where furniture used to retreat, and empty wren nests in corners nobody needs to hide in.

Mirrors turning away belong to Shame. Rounded corners come from wear, not covering (Mercifulness owns cloth bindings). Keeps the wren (Temperance to get another creature). Olive to Mercifulness; elephant dropped.
Baseness
Despair
Pig; trampled roses (as behaviour)
a cramped, scuffed house where everything is a little smaller and shabbier than it needs to be, and every slight is remembered.
a chair in the hall with one leg sawn short, kept for guests you dislike.
(C) Kick marks at shin height on doors and skirting. • (C) The last honey cake in the crock is always broken.
(U: first petty act) A grudge chest of potsherds, a slight scratched on each. • (C) The owner's initials scratched into furniture beside other people's. • (C) Ceilings sag a hand lower, room by room.

(C, pervasive) The house cramps inward and downward: rooms in the Despair wing shrink, and corners fill with junk nobody bothers to clear. • (C) A pig roots in the cellar; flowers that guests bring are found trampled in the hall by morning. • (U: crossing into Deep) A muttering in the walls repeats old slights, just too quiet to answer.
kick marks painted over badly, a grudge chest of sherds scratched blank, and the short-legged chair propped level on a sherd.
Realigned to pettiness and meanness (its deeds), away from earthy comfort, which overlapped Sensuality. Pig and trampled roses appear as behaviour. Sleeping hound belongs to Despondency.
Nobility
Hope
None kept (lion and Minerva dropped: no gods)
an upright hall of clean proportion that seems to stand for something, open to the sky and to strangers alike.
a small bronze of a nameless figure standing at ease on the hall table, gaze level, one hand open: the only ornament in the house.
(C) A clean draught of high, cool air from somewhere above, even in closed rooms. • (U: in stages, one word per selfless deed) A motto carved over the threshold, gaining a word at a time.
(C) A pair of eagles circles high over the house, wheeling above the open vaults.

(U then C, pervasive: crossing into Deep opens the great oculus over the Hope wing; further depth pierces lanterns through every ceiling) Daylight and starlight fall straight through the house. • (C) Plain linen banners stir down the halls in a wind that always seems to come from the horizon.
the oculus boarded over save one shaft of light; empty plinths whose footprints show where figures once looked out; the motto left unfinished mid-word.

Signature is a nameless bronze figure (the guest book is Good will's; Minerva dropped, as there are no gods). Eagles replace swifts (Audacity owns swifts). Window lamp, best room for guests and doors opening wider for the weary cut as duplicates of Good will, Fidelity and Meekness. Lion dropped.
Inflexibility
Grief
None kept (ass, lead weight and ivy dropped)
a house set in stone exactly as it was on one particular day, every object fixed where it was left.
a sundial in every room, the gnomon's shadow inlaid into the stone at the same hour, the true shadow ignored.

(C) A drip in the walls, steady as a water clock, that never varies by a hair. • (U: the first refusal of a companion's plea to change course) A cup on a table that can no longer be lifted, grown into the wood.

(C) Anything moved returns to its exact place by the next visit. • (C) A mineral crust, like the lip of a spring, creeps over objects left alone longest. • (C) Candle flames stand perfectly still, even when doors open.

(C, pervasive) Stillness spreads across the Grief wing and outward: curtains frozen mid-billow, water standing in poured arcs, a tossed coin hanging in the air. • (U: in stages, one object per vow kept against all reason) The mineral crust thickens until an object is fused to its place: a cushion, then the linens, then the bread on the laid table. • (U: crossing into Deep) Doors refuse any visitor who arrives by an unfamiliar route.
cracked mineral crusts beside the soft things they once encased, bolt holes where furniture stood fixed, and sundials each casting a true shadow at a different hour.

Owns objects returning to their place (Obduracy and Temperance no longer do it). Petrification belongs to Obduracy; Inflexibility fuses things with crust instead. Fixed sundials are distinct from Despondency's water clocks running dry. Ass, lead weight and ivy dropped (Fidelity owns ivy).
Malleability
Hope
Reed (pliant: woven willow)
a pliant, ever-rearranging house of curtains, reed screens and soft furniture that seems to reshape itself overnight for whatever might come.
a floor plan scratched in a wax tablet by the entrance, smoothed and redrawn so often the wax has gone soft.
(C) One screen stands a little differently on each visit. • (C) Woven willow chairs that give and spring back under weight.

(C) Corridors lengthen and shorten between visits; a three-step hall may take thirty. • (C) Knotted cord on handles, lamps and screen frames, every knot tied differently. • (U: the first time the player changes their mind on a major choice) The house begins guessing its guests: each visitor finds a chair shaped for them in the first room.

(C, pervasive) Rooms swap places overnight across whole floors, and the walls breathe, rippling like canvas in a breeze. • (U: crossing into Deep) A length of knotted cord runs along the walls and leads the way to wherever the house has moved things. • (U: each time the player adopts a new belief) A doorway appears where they most want one, then seals behind them with a soft seam.
empty rods where curtains once hung, plastered seams marking doorways that no longer open, and the floor plan finally incised in marble.
Cat given up (Good will owns the cat); knotted cord leads the way instead. Octopus dropped.
Cowardice
Fear
None kept (hare and abandoned shield dropped; dormice carry the flight)
a snug warren of small, padded rooms where every exit is known and nothing can surprise you.
a cushioned reading nook with a trapdoor beneath the cushion and a rope ladder neatly coiled beside it.
(C) doors latch themselves with a soft click a moment after you pass. (C) Small padded draught-stoppers lie at the foot of every door.

(C) latch bells tinkle faintly from rooms you have not yet entered, always one room ahead of you. (C) Dormice freeze, then bolt into the skirting, when approached. (U: first time the player flees a fight) a quilted texture begins creeping over hard surfaces, rounding corners; each later retreat spreads it one room further.

(C) across the whole house a muffling hush settles; footsteps vanish and any voice drops to a whisper on its own. (U: crossing into Deep) every room grows a second way out, an escape panel appearing in whichever wall you last looked at. (U: first guest after Deep) chairs turn to face the door and corridors fold so the guest keeps circling back to the entrance.
blanket nests left in empty alcoves, and doors studded with bolts and bolt plates that no longer fasten to anything.
Moths given up (Falseness keeps them); dormice instead. Hare and shield dropped.
Audacity
Courage
Icarus's wax wings (wax drips, stray feathers)
a soaring hall thrown open to the weather, built as if daring the sky to fall in.
a railless balcony jutting over nothing, one chair placed at its very lip.

(C) a breeze from nowhere lifts the loose ends of unrolled scrolls. (U: first reckless act that succeeds) one window that will never stay latched again. (C) Drips of old wax on the highest sills, and a stray feather now and then (Icarus).

(C) swifts nest in the highest vaults and scream as they dive through doorways; their number grows with depth. (C) Floorboards ring like drumskins underfoot. (U: each feat against long odds) a ledge sprouts from a wall at an odd height, and each climb leads somewhere real.

(C) indoor weather sweeps the Courage wing and every stairwell: wind, thunder rolling along the ceilings, rain falling into the atrium that floods nothing. (U: crossing into Deep) step out of a high window and a beam slides from the wall to meet your foot, then withdraws behind you. (U: first guest after Deep) guests are greeted by a gust that throws every shutter open at once.
wind-scoured grooves in the stone, an abandoned swift's nest, and a beam end jutting from an outer wall, sawn off short over the drop.
Owns swifts and indoor storms (Defiance's storm stays outside; Despondency's soft drizzle allowed).
Injustice
Hate
Hawk seizing a nightingale (Hesiod); broken scales
a lavish court where the finest room belongs to one, and everyone else crowds at its threshold.
a great scale in the entrance hall, permanently tipped, one pan resting on the floor heaped with polished stones.
(C) in every room one chair is plainly better than the rest, warmer and softer. (C) A heavy resinous incense scents only the favoured rooms.

(U: stages, at each new depth) a carved cameo of one crowned profile appears over lintels, then on drawer pulls, then pressed into the plaster. (U: first time the player takes a share meant for another) a pampered lapdog arrives to sleep before the hearth, its full bowl never shared. (C) A nightingale in a gilded cage sings only when the master enters. (C) Lesser rooms give up their best objects to the strongroom; their shelves thin as its hoard swells.

(U: crossing into Deep) the house grades whoever enters: the player glides along short, warm, polished ways, while guests come in by the narrow door and their corridors stretch long, cool and plain. (C) Heat and gloss drift toward a single centre like filings to a magnet. (C) A courtly echo repeats only the master's voice and swallows everyone else's.
bolt holes in the dais where the throne stood, and the entrance scale hanging level at last, one pan still dented from its old load.
Cats removed (Good will owns the cat). Hesiod's nightingale appears as a caged bird. Owns strongrooms (Greed has cases).
Justice
Courage
Scales in use (as plumb line and level)
a balanced, open hall where every room is the same size and every door has the same handle.
a plumb bob hanging dead centre over a floor inlay marking the exact middle of the house.

(C) a water-clock alarm pipe sounds the hour from the exact centre of the house, equally loud in every room. (U: first fair judgement the player makes between others) all the water clocks and sundials begin to agree to the second.
